name: link
title: Link
description: A navigation to another page or place, styled either inside running text or standing on its own.

inline.summary: A link inside a sentence. Always underlined, because colour alone does not distinguish it from the text around it.

tokens.rest · color: theme.accent-role.fg — verified AA-text on theme.bg.canvas, theme.bg.surface, theme.bg.subtle, theme.bg.muted, theme.accent-role.subtle and the success/warning/danger subtle backgrounds (L1)
tokens.hover / press: no change — the underline is already the affordance, and a colour shift mid-sentence reads as flicker; cursor: pointer only (L2)
tokens.focus · outline: focus.ring-width solid theme.focus-ring, offset focus.ring-offset, on :focus-visible (L3)
tokens.focus · wrapping: box-decoration-break: clone, so a link broken across lines gets a ring on each line (L3)

standalone.summary: A link on its own line or in a row of actions — 'View all', 'Back to invoices'. Not underlined, so it gets a box for the state layer.

tokens.focus: theme.focus-ring at focus.ring-width, offset focus.ring-offset, on :focus-visible — the same ring as inline (L7)

new-tab.summary: The glyph that says a link opens a new tab, sized from the text so it never outgrows the line.

tokens.announcement: the glyph is aria-hidden; '(opens in new tab)' is visually hidden text inside the link (L4)

behavior.summary: An `<a href>`, always. No primitive: the platform already owns a link's keyboard behaviour, and a router integrates by intercepting `onClick` while `href` stays real — the bargain TopNav and SideNav already make.

decisions.decision: A Link goes somewhere; a Button does something
decisions.why: The reader's expectations differ: a link can be opened in a new tab, copied and bookmarked, and is activated by Enter only; a button performs an action, is activated by Enter or Space, and has no address. Styling one as the other breaks those expectations for keyboard and screen-reader users while looking fine to everyone else. So `href` is required, there is no `onClick`-only Link, and an action styled as text is a tertiary Button.

decisions.decision: Inline links are always underlined, and get no hover change
decisions.why: WCAG 1.4.1: a link in a paragraph must be distinguishable by more than colour, and an underline that appears only on hover fails before the pointer arrives. With the underline always on, a hover change would be a hand-written `:hover` rule, which this system does not write. The state layer is the hover feedback everywhere else, but on inline text it would paint a box behind a phrase that wraps across lines — so inline links have none, and the cursor is enough. Standalone links have a box, so they compose the state layer like any other control.

A link with nowhere to go is not a disabled link, it is text. `aria-disabled` on an `<a>` without `href` is a pattern Pagination uses for its Previous and Next, where the row needs its shape; a free-standing link in that state is a puzzle for the reader. Render text, or render the link.

decisions.decision: `newTab` exists so the warning cannot be forgotten
decisions.why: WCAG 3.2.5 asks that a change of context be predictable, and a link that silently opens a new tab breaks Back for the reader who did not expect it. `newTab` sets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` together, and adds a glyph plus visually-hidden "(opens in new tab)" so it is announced. Passing `target="_blank"` by hand gets none of that, which is the reason this is a prop rather than an attribute the caller remembers.

Approved at gate 1 (decision C4, docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md). In an application most links are repeated navigation — the same invoices, the same settings — so a visited state would recolour half of every page and tell the reader nothing. A link is recognised by its underline, not its colour, so a visited colour would add no cue the reader needs. And it would be one more foreground to verify for contrast against every surface, in both schemes and every brand, while browsers deliberately limit what `:visited` can style for privacy. There is no visited token, none is to be proposed, and `:visited` gets no rule.

Web: an `<a href>`; `newTab` adds `target` and `rel`, a glyph and a visually-hidden suffix; a router intercepts `onClick` and calls `preventDefault`. React Native has no anchor: the link is a nested `Text` with `accessibilityRole="link"` and `onPress`, so it flows inside a paragraph, and `href` is opened with `Linking.openURL` unless the caller's `onPress` handles it for in-app navigation. `newTab` is web-only. `variant` works on both; the native state-layer equivalent is the `Pressable` pressed style, and the inline underline is `textDecorationLine: "underline"`. The OS's own text and link handling, not a Rata-drawn control (decision N5): the platform `Text` carries the link and `Linking` opens it; Rata supplies only the colour and underline. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

decisions.decision: Gate 2: every state's token mapping is approved
decisions.why: Approved state by state — L1 inline rest, L2 inline hover/press (no change), L3 inline focus, L4 the new-tab glyph, L5 standalone rest, L6 standalone hover/press (state layer), L7 standalone focus. Mapping it surfaced one gap: the link colour was verified on only three surfaces, while links also land in table rows, wells and Notices. theme.accent-role.fg was measured on theme.bg.subtle, theme.bg.muted and the three status subtle backgrounds — 4.89:1 or better in both schemes — and all five are now documented pairings that themes:check re-verifies for every brand (gate 2, docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).

use: A real URL, even inside a single-page app — the router intercepts `onClick`, and the address stays usable for new tabs and copying.
dont: `#` or `javascript:` to make a clickable thing. That is a Button.
href.a11y: A link without an `href` is not a link to the accessibility tree, which is why this is required.

children.summary: The link text — the name of where it goes.
use: Text that makes sense out of context: "View invoice INV-204".
dont: "Click here" or "Learn more" alone. Screen-reader users list a page's links, and a list of ten "Learn more"s is useless — name the destination, or extend the name with visually-hidden text.

variant.summary: Whether the link sits inside running text or on its own.
use: `standalone` for "View all" under a list, "Back to invoices" above a page, or a link in a row of actions.
dont: `standalone` inside a sentence. Without its underline it is distinguished from the text by colour alone.
variant.a11y: `inline` is always underlined, which is the non-colour cue WCAG 1.4.1 requires inside text.

newTab.summary: Opens the link in a new tab, and says so.
use: A link out of a task the reader must not lose — help docs opened from the middle of a form.
dont: Every external link, by habit. Opening a new tab takes Back away; the reader can choose a new tab themselves.
newTab.a11y: Adds a glyph and visually-hidden "(opens in new tab)", plus `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Web only.

use: Spacing a standalone link in its row.
dont: Removing the underline from an inline link, or recolouring it. Both undo the reason it is recognisable.

usage.when: A reference to another page, inside a sentence.
usage.example:
<Text>
  Contrast is verified per brand — see the <Link href="/docs/contrast">contrast report</Link>.
</Text>
usage.notes: `inline` is the default and is always underlined, so it is distinguishable without its colour.

usage.case: A standalone link with a client-side router
usage.when: "View all" under a preview list in a single-page app.
usage.example:
<Link
  variant="standalone"
  href="/invoices"
  onClick={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    navigate("/invoices");
  }}
>
  View all invoices
</Link>
usage.notes: `href` stays real, so middle-click and copy-link still work; the router only intercepts the plain click. The text names the destination rather than saying "View all" alone.

usage.when: Text that should trigger an action, such as "Resend code".
usage.notes: Don't. Nothing is navigated to, so it is a button: `<Button variant="tertiary" onClick={resend}>Resend code</Button>`, activated by Space as well as Enter and announced as what it is.
